item.description:
Chess & Balance fuses tactical chess with spell card magic. Cast spells. Move pieces. Chaos on the board. AI solved chess. It can't solve this. Ancient chess | Modern magic | Infinite strategies
♟️ Gameplay - is a 2-player card game that fuses standard chess with elemental spell decks. Each player picks one of five elements and uses 9 unique spell cards to summon pieces, protect their King, disrupt their opponent, and reshape the game. (Advance variants uses plasma for sideboard)
⚔️ HOW A TURN WORKS Each turn has two phases:- 🔮 Spell Phase (Optional), Play a card, cycle a card, or spend Spirits to summon new pieces onto the board.
- ♟️ Chess Phase (Mandatory), Make one standard chess move.
✦ SPIRIT is the resource that powers your deck. Every time your opponent plays a card, you gain Spirit equal to its cost. Higher-cost cards summon stronger pieces or trigger devastating effects.
🌟 THE FIVE ELEMENTS - 🔥 Fire - Aggressive removal and board disruption - 🌊 Water - Control, manipulation, card advantage - 🌿 Nature - Pawn swarming, promotion, King protection - 💨 Wind - Positional chaos, movement manipulation - ⚡ Plasma - Global persistent effects that reshape rules for BOTH players
🏆 OBJECTIVE Capture ALL of your opponent's Kings.
📦 WHAT'S IN THE BOX - 🃏 36 Spell Cards (9 Fire, 9 Water, 9 Nature, 9 Wind) - ⚡ 4 Sideboard Cards (4 Plasma x 2 players) - ♟️ 1 standard chess set and extra chess board for the extra pieces (not included) - 🪙 Tokens or coins for tracking Persistent Effects turns
📋 GAME DETAILS - 👥 Players: 2 - 🎯 Age: 8+ - ⏱️ Play Time: 30-120 minutes - 📖 Edition: Beta Edition
🌐 LEARN MORE - https://chessnbalance.com/ - https://www.thegamecrafter.com/games/chess-balance
BETA EDITION | JericoDP Design | AI Polish

This is a two player (black and white) abstract game played on a 13 square by 12 board. The two centre squares of the opposite long sides are coloured white and the rest of the squares are each coloured one of six other colours. Each player starts with 26 pieces, one king, two queens, two rooks four bishops, four knights and thirteen pawns. All except the king have a colour matching one or other of the board square colours and pieces start on the same rank as their king on their matching board square colour, pawns doing likewise on the second rank. Pieces mostly move as in chess but the king can move up to three squares, the object being to be first to get your king onto the opposing player's king's starting square. Pawns can be promoted to any piece that has been captured so that loss of your king is not necessarily fatal.

item.description:
The 32 pieces in Chex represent the 16 chess pieces on each side of a normal chess game. Each player shuffles his own 16 tiles and places them face down, then white draws his top tile and places it, with the piece oriented so it looks upright to him. Black then draws the top tile in his pile and places it so that it touches white's piece, either orthogonally or diagonally, and oriented so that it looks upright to him.
At that point, white can either add another piece or move his piece on the board. A move must be a legal chess move and may not separate any element of the board; all pieces much remain touching, even if just diagonally, when a move has ended. Thus you can "pin" a piece by placing a new piece on the far corner of a piece already in play.
The game ends in checkmate or stalemate, with a stalemate occurring when you must place your king into check when you draw it.
Chex was originally published in 1982 by IQ Products as Chess Cards. The rules in that version differ significantly from those in the later self-published version.

item.description: Chess Dungeon is chess-without-limits, created by Thomas P. W. James. Two or more people may play. Chess Dungeon applies the orthodox game language of Chess to an emergent playing space. It has no "board" as such - the playing area and the pieces that may be played are determined by custom, collectable playing cards. Each card may serve as either tiles of the "board" ("Land"), or be tabled ("Declared") to place the Chess pieces upon a Land card. Two cards are played per turn until players' cards run out. In this way players determine the size of the game (thus its approximate duration) by agreeing to how many cards may be played in a game. Players may also agree to different piece limitations and so forth. The aims are: be the last player alive (not checkmated), avoid stalemate, and win cards from other players in order to gain points.

item.description:
Chess Grand Prix is a fast-paced racing board game that transforms classic chess movement rules into an exciting competitive race experience.
Players take control of racing cars on a specially designed 50-space track inspired by a chessboard. Instead of traditional chess gameplay, movement is driven by dice rolls that activate chess piece abilities—Pawn, Knight, Bishop, Rook, Queen, and King—each offering unique movement patterns on the track.
The goal is not checkmate, but speed, strategy, and consistency. Players must complete 3 full laps while collecting points through racing positions, Pit Stop cards, and special action cards.
Strategic decisions are crucial: players must balance risk and reward, choose when to use advantage cards, and manage mandatory Pit Stop visits that can change the course of the race.
Key Features: Chess-inspired movement system (all piece movements are integrated into racing mechanics) Dice-driven tactical racing gameplay Card-based strategy system with 64 action cards and 24 Pit Stop cards Mandatory Pit Stop mechanic introducing risk management Dynamic track with special spaces and tactical shortcuts Point-based victory system rewarding both speed and strategy
Objective:
Complete 3 laps of the race track while collecting the highest total score from race positions, cards, and bonuses. The player with the highest score at the end of the final lap wins the Chess Grand Prix.
Design Purpose:
Chess Grand Prix is designed as an engaging way to teach chess movement rules through gameplay, especially for younger players. By integrating chess mechanics into a racing environment, players naturally learn how each chess piece moves while enjoying a competitive and fun board game experience.
—description from the designer

item.description:
Chess In The 3rd Dimension offers a challenge not to be found in standard chess games. Here, you play in three dimensions instead of two. Consequently, each player must "see" the game in terms of left and right, forward and back, as well as vertical up and down, as though the men on the field are suspended along three planes of space. You must be wary, as should your opponent, of being attacked from either above or below, as well as the other two dimensions.'
This chess game differs from a regular chess game in that it has three transparent boards stacked on top of each other. One player will start with his pieces on the top board, the other will have his pieces on the bottom board.
After their initial move, a piece automatically moves to the middle plane (with a few exceptions: a king or rook may remain on the same plane, as can a piece needed to prevent checkmate). From there on, each player can make a regular move or ascent or descent a single level (moving to the same square on a different level). When moving up or down, it is not possible to capture opposing pieces.

item.description:
Developed in Cebu City, Philippines, Chess Infinitum is a fantasy-based variant of chess played on a 10x10 checkerboard with its corner and its horizontally adjacent neighbor squares removed totaling 92 squares including the 2x2 "Infinitum squares" on the center of both sides.
As a chess variant, similarities with the original game include the piece moves being the same, existence of draw rules like stalemate, move repetitions and number-of-move rules, and promotion of a pawn reaching the other end of the board being present; however, major differences in gameplay include both sides only have 6 pawns, the starting position of the pieces are different, and the goal of the game is now to "capture" the opponent king instead of just checkmating it.
In addition, a piece placed on their own, differently colored, 2x2 "infinitum squares" can be moved as if they are occupying all other vacant squares in the said space. If another piece of yours has occupied one of the then-vacant squares in the "infinitum square" then those pieces will instead share the power of the remaining vacant squares. If all infinitum squares are occupied by a piece then this power becomes technically useless. You and your opponent cannot utilize the opposing infinitum squares but you could use one of your pieces to block its effect by occupying a square.
A more commonly used variant of the game is by adding the "Wizard" piece. This piece is initially placed on the player's infinitum square and moves similar to a Chess queen; its special power lies on it being uncapturable by the opponents king dealing a possible game-ending capture on the next move if not captured by another piece. Since it is a special piece, any pawn that promotes on the 9th or the 10th rank of the board cannot be promoted to a Wizard.

item.description:
Chess Joker brings elegant chaos to the classic game of Chess. The rules are quite simple: Play a normal game of chess, but with one extra twist — after each turn, flip the top card of the deck face up next to you. Each card depicts a Joker move, such as "Move your King like a Knight" or "Warp your Queen to deliver check". On your next turn, you can take a normal chess move, or use your card. If you don't use the card, it's gone, and you draw a new one. If you do use it, you score it for points. Accumulate 800 Elo worth of completed cards, and you win immediately — or exploit your cards' powers to deliver checkmate and win traditionally.
Each of the 256 cards in the game is unique, and they are divided into two 128 card sets: basic and advanced. Learning players can start with the basic cards, and introduce the rest when they're ready.
—description from the publisher
